subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: 3-D Printing: Additive Manufacturing
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: 3-D Printing: Additive Manufacturing.

hook.text: Instead of cutting material away, what if you add it layer by layer?

buildup.text: A nozzle or laser builds a part from plastic, metal, or ceramic one slice at a time.

discovery.text: Complex internal shapes that no tool could reach become trivial to make.

twist.text: Metal 3-D printing now makes rocket engine parts lighter than cast versions.

climax.text: Prototypes that took weeks to machine now print overnight on a desktop.

punchline.text: Layer by layer, manufacturing grows instead of shrinks.

quiz.question: What shapes can 3-D printing create that traditional machining can't?
options: Perfectly flat surfaces with no tool marks
Complex internal channels and hollow structures unreachable by cutting tools
Parts larger than the printer itself
